before.text:
Several remarks are immediate. First, the crossing symmetry is necessary. The original
unsymmetrized four-point function, written in terms of the Beta function, cannot be written
purely in terms of the zeta function. One needs to add in the full (s, t, u) symmetrization
of the four-point function. The moral here is: while three Gamma functions appropriately
combine into the Beta function (which was Veneziano’s initial observation), the appropriate
triple sum over the Beta functions gives us a ratio of pairs of Gamma functions. It is this
ratio which allows us, using the duality version (1.16) of the functional equation, to eliminate
the Gamma functions entirely in terms of ratios of zeta functions.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Derives the Li coefficients both from a transformed xi generating function and from derivatives at one, tying the paper's integral hierarchy back to equivalent canonical definitions.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The authors state these careful-factor formulas supersede their earlier integral representation; this local source supports only the displayed equivalence derivation.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy product differentiation; exact indices and factorial factors need text/scan checking.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Virasoro–Shapiro phase inherits the Volchkov criterion
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Rewrites the closed-string amplitude using zeta functional identities, relates it to the squared open-string amplitude with tangent factors, and derives a phase relation allowing substitution into the dressed criterion.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A zero-counting Stieltjes transform, the xi Hadamard invariant, and Chebyshev kernels organize the n=1 Volchkov equality as the first member of an all-n Li-coefficient family.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The exact all-n converse is formula-dense in this extraction and should be checked equation by equation before formal reuse.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Volchkov sits inside a Chebyshev–Li hierarchy

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Hadamard factorization makes three views of Li coefficients interchangeable: coefficients of a transformed xi logarithm, sums over zero-wise powers, and derivatives of z^(n-1)log xi at one.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Defining φ(z)=ξ(1/(1-z)) and substituting the xi Hadamard product gives a product whose logarithmic derivative generates the zero-sum coefficients kn. A Leibniz differentiation calculation then shows the same zero sum equals (n-1)!^-1 times the nth derivative of z^(n-1)log ξ(z) at z=1.
directed.conceptual_reading: A coordinate change converts zero locations into a power-series invariant, while differentiation supplies a local analytic representation of the same global zero sum.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The xi Hadamard product, the Möbius-transformed generating function, and derivatives at one bridge spectral zero data to canonical Li coefficients.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The span derives equivalence of the displayed coefficient representations only; it does not independently prove positivity, RH, or the preceding integral formulas.
directed.uncertainty: Product indices, convergence radius, factorials, and signs are formula-heavy and should be verified against the exact span before formal use.
